# Sorting by a field named index empties the collection

## Context

Found during the v13.3 manual sweep on `dev` `af81fc0f86`. In `examples/grid/covid`, one click on the sortable `#` header empties the grid. That column's `dataField` is `index`, which is a real `Integer` model field. The console then shows `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` for `'country'`, `'colspan'`, `'cases'` and `'annotations.selected'`. `apps/covid` and `apps/sharedcovid` declare the same `index` field.

## The Problem

`Neo.collection.Base#doSort` sorts through a map whenever a sorter has `useTransformValue`, and `Sorter` defaults that to true (`src/collection/Sorter.mjs:77`). So the map path is the default for every property sort. Each mapped entry starts as `{index}`, the item's position, and then takes each sort property as a key (`src/collection/Base.mjs:769–782`). A sort property named `index` overwrites the position with the item's own value. The map back, `items[el.index]` (`:805`), then looks items up by field value instead of position. An out-of-range value yields `undefined`, and an in-range one yields the wrong item. The covid data never sets `index`, so every entry becomes `undefined`, and every later read of the collection throws.

## The Architectural Reality

- The map is the "sorting with map" pattern cited at `:768`. Its position key shares one namespace with the sort properties.
- The direct path (`mappedItems = items`, when no sorter transforms) builds no helper object and is unaffected.
- `Store#doSort` hydrates and then calls `super.doSort`, so Stores and plain Collections share the defect.
- Design authority: a sort reorders a collection and never changes its members. The collection's own `sort` event reports `items` beside `previousItems` as the same set.

## The Fix

Key the position with a Symbol, declared beside `initialIndexSymbol` and `isSorted` at the top of `src/collection/Base.mjs`, so no string property can collide with it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit: a Collection sorted by a field named `index` (ASC, DESC, and as the second of two sorters) is ordered by that field and keeps every item. Red on `dev`.
- [ ] Unit: the same for a Store with raw items (`autoInitRecords: false`). Its complex-field hydration runs before `super.doSort` and only adds properties, so it never reaches the position key (Euclid's review note on #19802).
- [ ] `examples/grid/covid`: the `#` header sorts by `index` and keeps every row.
- [ ] The existing collection and data unit specs stay green.

## Out of Scope

- A `sortable: false` header that still sorts on click, #19801. That is how `apps/covid` reaches this defect through its non-sortable `#` column.
